message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Title | Year Published | Notes |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (also known as *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | The first book in the Harry Potter series; introduces Harry, Hogwarts, and the wizarding world. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Continues Harry’s second year at Hogwarts, featuring the mystery of the Chamber of Secrets. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map; a darker tone begins to emerge. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Features the Triwizard Tournament and the return of Voldemort. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Focuses on Harry’s fifth year, the rise of the Ministry’s influence, and the formation of Dumbledore’s Army. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince** | 2005 | Explores Voldemort’s past and sets up the final showdown. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Concludes the series with the epic battle at Hogwarts. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel, a political thriller set in a small English town. |
| **The Cuckoo’s Calling** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013 | Debut of the detective series featuring private investigator Cormoran Strike. |
| **The Silkworm** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2014 | Second book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Career of Evil** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2015 | Third book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Lethal White** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2018 | Fourth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable published as a free e‑book during the COVID‑19 pandemic. |

These titles cover the core Harry Potter saga, Rowling’s ventures into adult fiction, and her work under the pseudonym Robert Galbraith. Each has been widely read and critically acclaimed, making them staples of contemporary literature.
